title: Rapid fallback comms template (personal draft)
body:
TL;DR:
Personal scratch/template for quick internal + external messaging when we trigger model/region fallback or capacity-tier degradation. Goal: speed + clarity; leave room for team-specific bits.

Audience:
- Primary: engineers on-call, SRE triage leads, capacity ops
- Secondary: PMs owning affected product routes, comms leads, CSM on call for major customers

When to use:
- Auto-fallback triggered across >=2% of production traffic for >5 minutes
- Manual fallback during runway testing or preemptive capacity shift
- When latency p99 breaches SLA for a sustained window and we route to lower-capacity model variant

High-level structure (use this as the backbone for Slack + email + all-hands lines):
1) Situation (one sentence)
   - Example: "We detected increased queueing in us-west that caused automated routing to fall back to the compatibility model at 11:37 PT."
2) Impact (who + what)
   - Example: "~3% of requests for customer-facing text-generation routes may see longer latencies and slightly different response style. No data loss."
3) Mitigation (what we've done)
   - Example: "Traffic rerouted, canary rollback blocked, autoscale added N+1 on dedicated pools, and engineers are investigating the root cause."
4) Next steps and ETA
   - Example: "Investigating kernel contention pattern; expect update in 30 mins with either a rollback or capacity bump."
5) Ask (items requiring action and owners)
   - Example: "On-call: validate fallback logs (Ravi). Platform: provision burst nodes if p99 > 2s (Amelia). Comms: prepare external note if >15 mins (Iris)."
6) Where to follow (links + channels)
   - Incident channel, runbook link, dashboard link, customer escalation thread

Short Slack template (ops channel):
- SUBJECT: [INCIDENT] fallback -> compatibility-model in us-west (11:37 PT)
- BODY: "Brief: Auto-fallback triggered due to queueing; affecting ~3% prod traffic for text-gen routes. Mitigation: traffic routed to compatibility model; engineers triaging. Impact: latency p99 elevated; no data loss. ETA for next update: 30m. Action items: on-call to validate logs (Ravi), platform to consider burst nodes if p99 stays >2s (Amelia). Links: dashboard | runbook | customer-thread. I'll post a short external note if we cross 15m."

Short Email to internal stakeholders (PMs/CS/C-level):
Subject: Brief update: fallback event in us-west (11:37 PT)
Hi all,
We triggered an automated fallback at 11:37 PT in us-west due to transient queueing. About 3% of traffic for text-generation routes has been routed to the compatibility (lower-throughput) model. We have mitigations in place and no evidence of data loss. Engineers are actively investigating and we'll provide an ETA in 30 minutes. Please escalate customer concerns to the internal incident channel.
-- Iris

Customer-facing short blurb (if comms decides to notify customers quickly) – keep minimal and non-technical:
"We experienced a temporary performance issue in one of our regions that may have caused slower responses for a small subset of requests. Our systems automatically rerouted traffic to maintain availability and we're investigating the root cause. No customer data was affected. We'll post an update by [ETA]."

All-hands talking points (if execs need 60–90s script):
- What happened: "An automated fallback kicked in for a small portion of traffic in a US region due to internal queueing. We prioritized availability over latency by routing to a compatible model variant."
- Current status: "Systems are stable on the fallback variant; engineers are tracing root cause and validating full bandwidth restoration steps."
- Customer impact: "Small percentage of requests saw slower responses; no data integrity issues."
- Takeaway: "Our routing and fallback system worked as designed to keep customer-facing services online; we have concrete actions to reduce recurrence (capacity fixes + kernel/runtime patch)."

Engineer-facing checklist (quick actions to include in Slack or runbook updates):
- Attach trace IDs / request IDs to incident thread
- Capture kernel/GPU metrics + KV cache stats for impacted time window
- Confirm which model variant served traffic and sample outputs for QA review
- If suspect quantization mismatch, stash detailed sample + commit id
- Tag work in Jira INF-4127 for follow-up

Q&A (prep for PMs / CS):
Q: Did customer requests fail or data get lost?
A: No failures or data loss observed; requests were served by a compatible variant to preserve availability.

Q: Should we proactively notify customers?
A: If we cross 15 minutes or a key customer reports issues, yes. Otherwise we monitor and include in post-incident summary.

Q: Is this related to model quality drift?
A: Not likely — this was triggered by infrastructure queueing. We captured samples to confirm output fidelity.

Loose notes / placeholders I often forget to include:
- Who will own the post-incident RCA write-up? (Assign early)
- Timebox: make an interim update every 30 minutes during active incident
- Use 'compatibility model' phrasing internally to avoid detailed architecture explanation in early comms
- Shortlink list: dashboard | runbook | customer-thread (placeholders above)

Open questions I want to follow-up on (for myself):
- Can we surface a shorter p99 alert threshold specifically tied to routing fallbacks?
- Is the compatibility model telemetry automatically included in our per-route dashboards?
- Should we add a 'fallback reason' tag into request logs for faster triage?

Finish notes:
- This is my personal scratch/template — copy/paste and tweak as needed.
- Keep public wording conservative: prioritize availability, avoid technical blame, commit to timely updates.
- After incident: convert the best version of these lines into a polished internal/all-hands blurb and add to the incident page.

-- Iris (SRE)
